solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Yankee altering work on venue? It might happen

definitions.note: a whole phrase standing for the answer phrase, an admission that something is possible

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: altering says the letters of the following words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: An American is changing his plans for a venue, just in case something turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: Y comes first, then the eleven letters of WORK ON VENUE rearranged give OUNEVERKNOW.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when admitting an unlikely outcome remains possible, so it could happen.

clue.text: Remain outside a silent old prison

indicators.note: outside says the first piece goes around the pieces that follow it

parts.note: to be is to remain or continue, as in 'let it be'
still means silent, making no sound

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay quietly outside a disused jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remain' reads as the definition's verb, but here it is BE, as in 'let it be', which goes outside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress used as a state prison, stormed in 1789.

clue.text: Walk unevenly, drooping

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to walk favouring one leg

explanation.walkthrough: One word serves as a verb for an uneven gait and as an adjective for something sagging.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means hobbling on an injured leg; as an adjective it means slack and without firmness.

clue.text: Boss on outskirts of Idaho where TV show is made?

parts.note: a boss is a raised ornamental knob, also called a stud

indicators.note: outskirts of means only the outermost letters of Idaho are used, its first and last

explanation.surface: A manager visiting the edge of an American state where a television programme is filmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager but here is the decorative knob on a shield or ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Television programmes are recorded in a studio, a room equipped for filming and broadcasting.

clue.text: She's a devil getting head to support protest

indicators.note: to support means that in a down answer this piece sits beneath the other one, holding it up

parts.note: a demo is a protest march or demonstration
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour place names like Sheerness

explanation.surface: A wicked woman leads a protest, taking the front of it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer NESS goes below DEMO, so it supports it. A ness is a headland, a word found in British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A demoness is a female demon, so a she-devil fits the phrase.

clue.text: See about home floor covering

indicators.note: about says the first word's letters go around the second piece

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
in means at home

explanation.surface: An instruction to look into flooring for the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Lino, short for linoleum, is a smooth sheet material laid on kitchen floors.

clue.text: Giraffe-like animal comfortable with a Greek character

parts.note: OK means all right, comfortable
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An animal resembling a giraffe is at ease alongside a letter from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi of the Congo forests is the giraffe's only living relative, with a similar shape and striped legs.

clue.text: Article by investigator's about time in hellish place

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: about says the investigator's letters go around the next piece

parts.note: PI is a private investigator; with the 's it becomes PIS

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece beside a detective's account of time spent in an inferno.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling somewhere 'the pits' is slang for the worst possible place, as bad as hell.

clue.text: Horse somewhere in East Anglia one associated with Judy

parts.note: Suffolk is a county in East Anglia, eastern England
Punch is Judy's partner in the traditional Punch and Judy puppet show

explanation.surface: A horse found somewhere in eastern England, paired with a puppet show's heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Suffolk is an English county; Punch and Judy is a British seaside puppet show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suffolk Punch is a breed of heavy draught horse, chestnut in colour.

clue.text: Jotter from famous college brought back home

indicators.note: brought back says these letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school, Eton College
pad is slang for one's home or flat

explanation.surface: A notebook taken home from a well-known school.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is an elite English boarding school near Windsor, the crossword's favourite 'famous college'.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a pad of paper for writing notes on, which a jotter is too.

clue.text: Some icon of fashion not constant

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A style icon whose influence comes and goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on-off is intermittent, switching between states rather than staying steady.

clue.text: Dicky loved Italian city's cycling stadium

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or faulty, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital; the 's is the link 'has'

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky loved the Italian capital's track for bikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but is British slang for unsound, signalling the rearrangement of LOVED to VELOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A velodrome is an arena with a banked oval track built for track cycling races.

clue.text: Poet laureate once twenty-four hours on Scottish isle

parts.note: a day lasts twenty-four hours
Lewis is an island in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland

explanation.surface: A former national poet spending a day on a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Day-Lewis held the UK's official laureateship from 1968 until his death in 1972.

clue.text: Show disapproval of incomplete tome

indicators.note: incomplete says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Jeering at an unfinished volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To boo something is to jeer at it, expressing disapproval loudly.

clue.text: Fractured rib racing with bikes on some French peninsula

indicators.note: fractured means broken, so the letters of rib are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
any means some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: An injured motorcyclist with a broken rib on a peninsula in France.
explanation.walkthrough: RIB rearranged gives BRI. The TT is the Isle of Man motorbike race series.
explanation.definitionFit: Brittany is the region on the large peninsula of north-west France jutting into the Atlantic.

clue.text: Track English whisky

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Tracking down a whisky from England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a spirit distilled mainly from rye grain, a type of whisky popular in America and Canada.

clue.text: Standard cart reversed by Rod

indicators.note: by means next to, so the stick is placed right beside the reversed cart in the answer
reversed says the cart's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a dray is a low flat cart for heavy loads
a stick is a rod

explanation.surface: A cart backed up next to a man named Rod, as a benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a measure by which others are judged, a benchmark or criterion.

clue.text: New store runs rota

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters of store are reshaped

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A newly opened shop operates a staff schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster and a rota are both lists showing who is on duty when.

clue.text: Relative getting drug in French resort

indicators.note: in says the drug goes inside the resort's name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A family member taking drugs on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family relation.

clue.text: Aristocrat left overwhelmed by attention

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means, in a down answer, this piece lies underneath the other one

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A noble who departed, swamped by all the notice he got.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking above a viscount, a member of the peerage.

clue.text: Therapeutic massage — it has relaxed us in retirement

indicators.note: relaxed means loosened, so the letters of it has are loosened and rearranged
in retirement means going back, so the word us is read backwards

explanation.surface: A massage that has eased us in our old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests old age, but here it means withdrawing, going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiatsu is a Japanese form of bodywork using finger pressure on points of the body.

clue.text: Winos that regularly scrap

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter of the words, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Drunks who habitually fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a verb about fighting but is the noun for a tiny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota is a tiny amount, a jot, after the smallest Greek letter.

clue.text: Period of fighting harsh, reflected by American magazine

indicators.note: by means beside, so the magazine's title is placed right after the reflected word
reflected means mirrored, so the letters of harsh's synonym are read backwards

parts.note: raw can mean harsh, as in a raw wind
Time is a US news magazine

explanation.surface: A tough stretch of combat reported in an American magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Wartime is the duration of a war, an era of combat.

clue.text: Group of workers reportedly steal clothing item

parts.note: TU stands for trade union, a group of workers

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for steal is heard rather than read, giving a spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: nick is British slang for steal

explanation.surface: Union members said to be pinching garments.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick, British slang for steal, is only heard here, so it is written NIC to finish the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose garment reaching the hips or knees, also a uniform jacket.
